title: Bad Universal Priors and Notions of Optimality
version: COLT 2015 PDF; author-source archive arXiv v1 (2015-10-16)
publication_review_status: Peer-reviewed conference paper with author-source deposit
formal_verification_status: Reconstructed the posterior mixture and first-deviation inequality in Theorem 7. Verified a two-environment example with exact rational Bellman recursion at horizons 1, 2, 3 and 8. Independently checked the lifetime qualifications against Definitions 3–4 and the cited UAI paper. No proof assistant was used.
reading_progress: Read the complete 16-page PMLR PDF (proceedings pp. 1244–1259). Covered §§1–2, §§3.1–3.2, all proofs/corollaries in §§4–5, §§6.1–6.3, Figure 1, Tables 1 and 3, references on PDF pp. 12–14, Appendix A notation and Appendix B (compiler lengths, Lemma 19 and Theorem 11). Checked the Pareto proof and ergodic-horizon exception in Hutter 2002, and the finite-lifetime quantifier in Leike–Hutter UAI 2015 §3.2 and Theorem 14. Other cited works were reviewed as references within the article.
mathematical_topics: Universal prior sensitivity; off-policy nonidentification; Pareto optimality
extracted_instruments: In Theorem 7 an adverse environment copies the universal baseline on every history consistent with a given computable policy π and pays zero forever on first deviation. The mixture posterior keeps baseline weight ε/(1+ε). A deviation has value at most that weight, so V_baseline^π(h)>ε forces a unique default action. Finite witness: the default pays 1/2 in both environments. The alternative pays 1 forever in the true environment (prior 1/5) and zero forever after deviation in the adverse environment (prior 4/5). The observed default has exact value 1/2 forever, yet the true optimal gain over it is 1/2 per round. Theorem 18 supplies a finite-state environment which rewards one policy after its first consequential divergence. This witness isolates the posterior mechanism in two environments. The paper’s construction uses an actual universal baseline. The finite-lifetime correction requires Γ_(|h|+1)>0, an available positive reward and a zero-reward percept for punishment. At length m all actions tie. The p. 8 nonattainment statement also requires an infinite horizon or uniformity over m. A finite table attains the optimum for each fixed m.
fp_relevance: Agreement on actions actually taken leaves counterfactual outcomes underdetermined. A score averaged under a chosen universal mixture can favor an arbitrary computable policy. Apply the argument to an explicitly stated task distribution, feedback and exploration regime. The paper puts code-length bounds on compilers and a value cost on deviations. It does not quantify decision time, memory, training work, physical acquisition cost or transfer to a specified new task distribution.

mathematical_topics: Off-policy evaluation; importance ratios; doubly robust estimators
extracted_instruments: Equations (4)–(5) give cumulative action-probability ratios. Equation (10) cancels the baseline in conditional expectation with known logging propensities, target coverage and target and baseline independent of evaluation draws. If a target takes b at all H rounds, the logger takes b independently with probability p and only the all-b leaf has Bernoulli(m) reward, each trajectory's score has Fisher information p^H/[m(1−m)]. Any regular estimator unbiased through this family has variance at least m(1−m)/(n p^H). DR with a fixed baseline equal to the true Q at the evaluation parameter reaches the bound pointwise.
